lesson_title: The Man Who Stopped the Desert
hook_text: A farmer with a hoe and a pile of manure turned desert into forest, and his method costs almost nothing.
clip_script: Burkina Faso. Hard, bare ground where nothing grows. Yacouba Sawadogo picks up a hoe. He digs small pits, fills them with manure, and plants seeds. The pits catch every drop of rain. Termites tunnel in, letting water soak deep. Year after year, crops grow, then trees, then a forest. That's appropriate technology: cheap, simple, local, and kind to the land. You can try it too. Poke holes in a plastic bottle, bury it by a plant, and you have drip irrigation. Plant maize, beans and pumpkins together, and they help each other grow. Turn scraps into compost. Grow sorghum and morogo that laugh at drought. Collect rain from the roof in a tank. You don't always need a giant tractor to grow more food.
visual_style: Cracked earth in the Sahel; a farmer digging small pits; seedlings rising from the pits; a green forest; a bottle drip-feeding a tomato plant; a school food garden with maize, beans and pumpkins; a compost heap; a bowl of morogo.
pacing: Slow and patient for the desert story, then quick practical tips.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn about appropriate technologies and farming techniques that boost food security.
